The action line is drawn 4 hours to the right of the alert line. (Book p506)
Types of partogram: Friedman curve, modified WHO & Labour Care Guide
Fill up: The Friedman curve plots cervical dilatation against time, while the modified WHO partograph adds the ______ line and the ______ line to it.
The alert line shows the expected rate of progress and the action line, four hours to its right, is the point at which intervention is required. (Book p506)
Which of the following statements about Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters is TRUE?
Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters — 30 min; 15 min; 110–160 bpm
Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters — 15 min; 5 min; 120–160 bpm
Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters — 60 min; 30 min; 100–160 bpm
Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters — 30 min; 30 min; 110–150 bpm
FHR normal 110–160 bpm, recorded every 30 min (every 15 min for high risk). (Book p506)
All of the following are Modified WHO partograph: upper (fetal) parameters EXCEPT:
Intact membrane : colourless fluid : meconium stained : blood stained
Intact : clear : mixed : bloody — I = intact membrane; C = colourless; M = meconium stained; B
Intact : cloudy : meconium : bile — I = intact membrane; C = colourless; M = meconium stained; B
I = intact membrane; C = colourless; M = meconium stained; B = blood stained. (Book p506)

A 28-year-old woman at 30 weeks with modified who partograph: upper (fetal) parameters presents with on the partograph, moulding is recorded as 0 or × for none and +1, +2, +3 for increasing degrees of . Moulding on the partograph is denoted as:?
0 or × for none; +1, +2, +3 for degrees of overlapping of cranial bones
0 or × for none; +1, +2, +3 for degrees of caput succedaneum
A, B and C grades for degrees of overlapping of the cranial bones
I, C, M and B grades recorded against each hourly observation
On the partograph, moulding is recorded as 0 or × for none and +1, +2, +3 for increasing degrees of overlapping of the cranial bones. (Book p506)
All of the following are recorded in the upper part of the modified WHO partograph EXCEPT:
Colour and character of the amniotic fluid
Degree of moulding of the fetal skull
The upper part follows the fetus — heart rate, membranes, liquor and moulding; maternal observations belong to the lower part. (Book p506)
Fill up: In the modified WHO partograph, the interval for fetal parameters is represented by one small box equal to ______, and the three parts of the sheet are ______. is ______.
30 min; upper = fetal parameters, middle = cervicograph, lower = maternal condition
1 hr; upper = maternal, middle = fetal, lower = drugs
15 min; upper = cervicograph, middle = contractions, lower = fetal
2 hr; upper = drugs, middle = fetal, lower = maternal
One small box = 30 min for fetal parameters; upper part fetal, middle part cervicograph, lower part maternal condition. (Book p507)
Which of the following statements about Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones is TRUE?
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones — Cervicograph
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones — Tocograph
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones — Cardiograph
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones — Friedman graph
Middle part = cervicograph (cervix plotted as X, descent as O; 1 box = 1 hour). (Book p507)
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
Match the cervicograph zone to its meaning — green : yellow (alert) : pink (action).
Normal progress : alert, so shift her to a tertiary centre : intervene once the action line is touched
Alert, so shift her : normal progress : intervene on touching the action line
Intervene at once : alert, so shift her : entirely normal progress
Normal progress : intervene at once : refer her to a tertiary centre
Green means progress is normal, the alert zone means prepare for transfer, and touching the action line means intervention is required. (Book p507)
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
The colour-coded zones form the basis of the ______ WHO partogram.
The zones are the basis for the simplified WHO partogram. (Book p507)
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
The first plotting of cervical dilatation is always made:
On the alert line (never to the left of it)
To the left of the alert line
First plot is always on the alert line > left of alert line. (Book p507)
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
Worked example from the notes: a G2P woman at 4 cm at 4 pm is plotted on the alert line; at 6 pm she is 6 cm and at 8 pm 8 cm. Her progress is:
Normal progress (1 cm/hr, staying left of/on the alert line)
Alert zone – refer to tertiary centre
4 → 6 → 8 cm over 4 hours = 1 cm/hr, plotted on/left of the alert line = normal progress. (Book p507)
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
Fill up: The alert line on the cervicograph is drawn at a dilatation rate of ______ cm per hour from the point of admission, and the action line lies ______ hours to its right.
Crossing the action line means slow progress has persisted for four hours and transfers, augmentation or operative delivery must be considered. (Book p507)
Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
Which patient parameters are NOT recorded on the modified WHO partograph?
Respiratory rate, SpO2 and oral fluids consumed
Not recorded: respiratory rate, SpO2, oral fluids consumed. (Book p508)
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
Adequate uterine contractions are defined as:
At least three in 10 minutes, each lasting 45 seconds and raising pressure by 65-75 mmHg
At least five in 10 minutes, each lasting 60 seconds at 100 mmHg
At least two in 10 minutes, each lasting 20 seconds at 30 mmHg
At least three in 15 minutes, each lasting 30 seconds at 50 mmHg
Adequate contractions are three or more in ten minutes, each lasting about 45 seconds with an amplitude of 65-75 mmHg. (Book p508)
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
Contractions are measured by observation over the uterine fundus for ______ every ______.
Observed over fundus for 10 minutes every 30 minutes. (Book p508)
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
More than 5 contractions in 10 min is termed:
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
Match the shading of contraction duration boxes – dotted : hatched/oblique lines : solid fill.
Dotted <20 sec; hatched 20–40 sec; solid >40 sec (each box = 1 contraction). (Book p508)
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
A contraction lasting ≥60 sec indicates ______; management is ______.
A hypertonic contraction from oxytocin; stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, consider terbutaline
An entirely adequate contraction, so the infusion should be continued unchanged
Tachysystole, for which the rate of oxytocin should be increased
A Bandl's ring forming, which requires immediate caesarean section
A contraction lasting 60 seconds or more is hypertonic and usually drug-induced: stop the infusion, turn her and give a tocolytic if needed. (Book p508)
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions

Match the lower-part observation with how it is recorded — 1) Uterine contractions 2) Maternal pulse 3) Urine … A) Five squares per hour shaded according to the duration and strength of each contraction B) Recorded hourly and entered as a dot on the chart C) Recorded at each voiding, with the volume and any protein or acetone noted
Contractions fill five squares an hour, the pulse is plotted hourly, and urine is checked at each void for volume, protein and ketones. (Book p508)
Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
Arrange the seven sections of the Labour Care Guide in order (Sections 1–7):
Patient & labour details → supportive care → care of baby → care of woman → labour progress → medication → plan of action
Care of woman → care of baby → supportive care → labour progress → medication → plan → details
Labour progress → medication → plan → details → supportive care → baby → woman
Details → baby → woman → supportive care → medication → progress → plan
1 details, 2 supportive care, 3 baby, 4 woman, 5 labour progress, 6 medication, 7 plan of action. (Book p508)
Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
The mnemonic for the LCG sections given in the notes is:
Please Save Big Women Lovingly Made
Mnemonic: Smart Beautiful WOMEN Love Me. (Book p509)
Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
Which statements describe the Labour Care Guide layout and applicability?
Alert box in front of each parameter; used in all women in labour; used at all levels of health care
Alert line drawn diagonally; used only in high-risk women; tertiary centres only
No alert boxes; primigravida only; primary centres
Action line retained; multigravida only; secondary centres
LCG has an alert box before each parameter, is used for all women in labour and at all levels of care. (Book p509)
Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
Section 2 (Supportive care) of the LCG includes:
Companion, posture, oral fluid (solid food not advisable), pain relief
Supportive care: companion, posture, oral fluid (solids not advisable) and pain relief. (Book p509)
Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
Using the WHO Labour Care Guide, a woman at 6 cm moves into the alert column because dilatation has slowed. Contractions are adequate and the fetal heart is normal. What does the guide advise?
Document the deviation, look for and treat the cause, and continue supportive care with closer monitoring
Immediate caesarean section for every entry into the alert column
Reassurance only, because the alert column carries no clinical meaning
Stop monitoring and transfer her out of the labour ward
The alert column is a prompt to reassess and respond to the underlying cause rather than a trigger for automatic surgery. (Book p509)
Labour Care Guide: supportive care & alert column
Coding for companion, oral fluid and pain relief in the LCG – Y : N : D; which one is an alert feature?
Yes : No : Denied; 'N' is the alert
Yes : None : Done; 'D' is the alert
Young : Normal : Delayed; 'Y' is the alert
Y = yes, N = no (alert), D = denied. (Book p510)
Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
Posture coding in the LCG – MO : SP : L/L; the alert feature is:
Mobile : supine : left lateral; supine is the alert
Motionless : sitting : lying; sitting is alert
Mobile : semi-prone : lateral; lateral is alert
MO mobile, SP supine (alert), L/L left lateral. (Book p510)
Labour Care Guide: sections, supportive care & alert column
In LCG Section 3, baseline FHR normal is ______, abnormal (alert) is ______, documented every ______.
Normal 110–160; alert <110 or >160; documented every 30 min as per WHO guideline. (Book p510)
FHR deceleration codes – N : E : L : V; which is the alert feature?
No : early : late : variable; late is the alert
None : early : light : very; variable is the alert
Normal : early : late : variable; early is the alert
No : elevated : low : varied; low is the alert
N no, E early, L late (alert), V variable. (Book p510)
Amniotic fluid codes in the LCG and alert features:
I intact and C clear; M meconium-stained and B blood-stained are alerts
I intact and C clear; both codes are alerts on the chart
I inadequate and C clear; M is a normal finding here
Only C clear is recorded, and I is treated as an alert
In the Labour Care Guide the amniotic fluid codes are I for intact and C for clear, while M (meconium-stained) and B (blood-stained) are alerts. (Book p510)
Fetal position codes – A : P : T; alerts are:
Occipitoanterior : occipitoposterior : occipitotransverse; P and T are alerts
Anterior : posterior : transverse; only P is alert
Anterior : posterior : transverse; A is alert
Asynclitic : posterior : transverse; T is alert
A = OA; P = OP (alert); T = OT (alert). (Book p510)
Caput and moulding are coded as +/++/+++; the alert feature is:
Caput/moulding +++ is the alert feature. (Book p510)
Which of the following statements about the WHO Labour Care Guide is TRUE?
It records fetal heart rate, liquor, caput and moulding in the section on the baby, and its alert column prompts a clinical response
It replaces the partograph and no longer records the fetal heart rate
It is intended only for women with obstructed labour or ruptured uterus
It recommends routine amniotomy for every woman as soon as she reaches 4 cm
The Labour Care Guide keeps continuous fetal and maternal observation but replaces rigid time limits with alert thresholds and individualised care. (Book p510)
LCG Section 3: care of the baby
Section 4 (care of woman) records pulse, temperature, BP and urine (protein, acetone). Match the alert thresholds – pulse : systolic BP : diastolic BP : temperature.
Alerts: pulse <60/≥120; SBP <80/≥140; DBP ≥90; temp <35.0/≥37.5 °C; urine P++/A++. (Book p511)
LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
Section 5 (progress of labour) – contraction alerts: number in 10 min ______ and duration ______.
Alert: ≤2 or >5 contractions per 10 min; duration <20 or >60 seconds (checked every 30 min). (Book p511)
LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
Time-bound alert figures for cervical dilatation in the LCG – at 5 cm : 6 cm : 7 cm : 8 cm : 9 cm.
Time-bound alerts: 5 cm → 6 h, 6 → 5, 7 → 3, 8 → 2.5, 9 → 2 h (mnemonic 6-5-3-2.5-2); at 10 cm second stage, P = time of pushing. (Book p511)
LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
WHO maximum duration of second stage – primi without epidural : multi without epidural : with epidural.
Primi 3 h, multi 2 h; add 1 h with epidural. (Book p511)
LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
Section 6 (medication) of the LCG records ______ and Section 7 is ______.
Oxytocin, IV fluids and drugs given; shared decision-making and plan
Antibiotics and referral details only; shared decision-making and plan
Analgesics and fluids given; discharge summary and follow-up plan
Tocolytics and drugs given; newborn care and feeding plan recorded
Section 6 of the Labour Care Guide records medication (oxytocin, IV fluids, drugs) and Section 7 records shared decision-making – assessment and plan. (Book p511)
LCG Sections 4–7: woman, progress, medication & plan
All of the following are recorded in the WHO Labour Care Guide EXCEPT:
A postnatal follow-up plan for six weeks after delivery
Maternal position, mobility, hydration and pain relief
Progress of labour with dilatation, descent and contractions
Medications given and the plan for the next review
The guide covers the woman, the baby, progress, medication and the plan for labour itself; postpartum follow-up is a separate schedule. (Book p511)
Labour is defined as the process by which a fetus, after attaining ______, is expelled from the ______.
Labour = process by which a fetus after attaining the period of viability is expelled from the genital tract. (Book p512)
Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
All of the following are among the five criteria for normal labour EXCEPT:
Delivery by caesarean section if the labour becomes prolonged
Term gestation, that is 37 to 42 completed weeks
Vertex presentation with an uncomplicated vaginal delivery
The five criteria are spontaneous onset, term gestation (37-42 weeks), vertex presentation, uncomplicated delivery and vaginal delivery. (Book p512)
Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour

Match the phase of parturition with what characterises it — 1) Phase 1, uterine quiescence 2) Phase 2, myometrial activation 3) Phase 4 … A) The postpartum phase B) Unresponsive uterus, soft cervix, progesterone the main hormone C) Functional progesterone withdrawal with cervical ripening

Phase 1 is quiescence with an unresponsive uterus, soft cervix and progesterone dominant; phase 2 is activation with functional progesterone withdrawal, more oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors, more gap junctions and cervical ripening; phase 4 is the postpartum phase. (Book p512)
Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
All of the following occur in phase 2 of parturition, the myometrial activation phase, EXCEPT:
Functional withdrawal of progesterone with a rise in estrogen
More oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors with more gap junctions

Phase 2 is functional withdrawal of progesterone, a rise in estrogen, more oxytocin and prostaglandin receptors, more gap junctions and cervical ripening — not a rise in progesterone action. (Book p512)
Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
Match phase 3 and phase 4 of labour:
Phase 3 = uterine stimulation/contraction (all stages of labour); Phase 4 = postpartum phase
Phase 3: uterine stimulation – all stages of labour included; Phase 4: postpartum. (Book p512)
Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
Fill up: The fetal cascade for the onset of labour runs from fetal hypothalamic ______ to pituitary ACTH to fetal adrenal ______ and then to placental estrogen.
The cascade is hypothalamic CRH, pituitary ACTH, fetal adrenal DHEA-sulfate, conversion to estrogen in the placenta and then uterine contractions. (Book p512)
Definition, criteria & the four phases of labour
Fill up: Labour is defined by painful uterine contractions that produce progressive ______ and ______ of the cervix.
softening; shortening of the lower segment
Contractions alone are not enough; the cervix must show progressive effacement and dilatation for the diagnosis of true labour. (Book p512)
Fill up: Lightening is descent of the fetal head into the pelvis, which causes a ______ in fundal height and relieves ______.
Lightening is descent of the head into the pelvis, lowering the fundal height and relieving respiratory distress. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
Which statement about cervical ripening before labour is TRUE?
Ripening reduces cross-linking of fibres and raises water content and hyaluronic acid
Ripening increases cross-linking and reduces water content and hyaluronic acid
Ripening increases collagen deposition and reduces the water content
Ripening increases elastin and reduces the amount of hyaluronic acid
Ripening is due to prostaglandins and connective-tissue change: less cross-linking of fibres, more water content and more hyaluronic acid. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
Which statement about true versus false labour pain is TRUE?
True labour contractions are regular and progressive in strength; false labour pains are neither
True labour contractions are irregular and continuous; false labour pains are regular and rhythmic
True labour contractions continue at a fixed intensity; false labour pains are rhythmic and progressive
True labour contractions are regular but decreasing; false labour pains are progressive and rhythmic
True labour contractions are regular and increase in frequency, duration and intensity; false labour pains do neither. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain

Match the feature of labour with the type of labour it belongs to — 1) Site of the pain 2) Show and bag of membranes 3) Response to sedation, enema and rest … A) Relieved by sedation in false labour, not relieved in true labour B) Lower abdomen radiating to the back of the thigh in true labour C) Show present and membranes felt in true labour

True labour pain is in the lower abdomen radiating to the back of the thigh, the show is present and the bag of membranes is felt, and it is not relieved by sedation; false labour does not radiate, has no show, and is relieved by sedation, enema and rest. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
Fill up: In true labour the show is ______ and the bag of membranes ______; in false labour neither is found.
In true labour the show is present and the bag of membranes is felt; in false labour the show is absent and the membranes are not felt. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
Fill up: False labour pains are ______ by sedation, enema and rest, whereas true labour pains are ______.
False labour pains respond to sedation, enema and rest; true labour pains do not. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain

Match the pattern with its meaning — 1) True labour 2) False labour 3) Pre-labour or prodromal phase … A) Irregular contractions that do not intensify and settle with rest or sedation B) Regular contractions increasing in frequency and intensity with cervical change C) Cervical ripening with a show and irregular pains before active labour begins
False labour settles with rest and does not change the cervix; the prodromal phase is the uncomfortable run-up to real labour. (Book p513)
Pre-labour state & true vs false labour pain
Fill up: The three Ps required for labour are ______, ______ and ______.
The 3 Ps are Push, meaning uterine contractions, Passage, meaning the pelvis, and Passenger, meaning the baby. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions

Match each feature of uterine contractions with its value — 1) Origin 2) Speed of spread 3) Time to depolarise the whole uterus 4) Predominant site … A) 2 cm per second B) Fundus C) Cornua D) 15 seconds
Contractions originate in the cornua, spread at 2 cm per second, take 15 seconds to depolarise the entire uterus, and are predominant at the fundus. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
Fill up: Palpable ______ mmHg, painful 15 mmHg, cervical dilatation 20–25 mmHg.
Palpable 10 mmHg, painful 15 mmHg, cervical dilatation 20–25 mmHg. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions

A 28-year-old second gravida at 12 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions. According to the notes, 1st stage 40–50 mmHg; 2nd/3rd stage 100–120 mmHg; basal tone 10–20 mmHg; monitored every 30 min. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
Advise that 40–50 mmhg : 100–120 mmhg : 10–20 mmhg is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 100–120 : 40–50 : 5 mmhg is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 20–25 : 40–50 : 10 mmhg is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 60–75 : 120–150 : 20–30 is the correct the 3 ps & physiology of uterine contractions for this patient at this gestation
1st stage 40–50 mmHg; 2nd/3rd stage 100–120 mmHg; basal tone 10–20 mmHg; monitored every 30 min. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
Fill up: 1 MVU = ______ (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min; adequate = 200–220 MVU.
Strength of contraction (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min
1 MVU = strength (mmHg) × number of contractions in 10 min; adequate = 200–220 MVU. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
Fill up: Upper segment = ______ uterus (contracts); lower segment = isthmus (passively dilates); effaced cervix becomes part of LUS. Blood flow to uterus ↓ during contractions.
Entire uterus; contracts; isthmus; passively dilates; lower uterine segment
Isthmus; dilates; fundus; contracts; upper segment
Upper segment = entire uterus (contracts); lower segment = isthmus (passively dilates); effaced cervix becomes part of LUS. Blood flow to uterus ↓ during contractions. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
Fill up: The three Ps that determine the outcome of labour are ______.
Uterine powers, the fetus as passenger and the maternal bony passage together decide whether labour will be normal or obstructed. (Book p514)
The 3 Ps & physiology of uterine contractions
Fill up: Tachysystole = ______/10 min; m/c cause misoprostol > oxytocin.
Tachysystole = >5 contractions/10 min; m/c cause misoprostol > oxytocin. (Book p514)

Match the tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions with the correct detail — 1) The consequence of tachysystole and its CTG picture 2) Management sequence of tachysystole: 3) Precipitate labour is defined as completion of the … A) Fetal distress due to ↓ blood supply; prolonged deceleration B) Stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, give oxygen, fluids if needed, then terbutaline C) <3 hours; perineal tear, hematoma, PPH
Consequence: fetal distress (↓ blood supply); CTG shows prolonged deceleration. (Book p514)
All of the following are Tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions — Management sequence of tachysystole: EXCEPT:
Fetal distress due to ↓ blood supply; prolonged deceleration
Stop the oxytocin, turn her to the left, give oxygen, fluids if needed, then terbutaline
Tachysystole is managed by stopping the oxytocin, repositioning, oxygen and fluids, with a tocolytic such as terbutaline if it persists. (Book p514)
Fill up: Precipitate labour: entire process ______ h → perineal tear, hematoma, PPH.
Precipitate labour: entire process <3 h → perineal tear, hematoma, PPH. (Book p514)

A 30-year-old G3P1L1 at 12 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions. According to the notes, hypotonic contractions lead to prolonged or slow progress of labour and are managed by augmentation with artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
Advise that prolonged slow progress of labour; augmentation with arm and oxytocin is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that fetal distress from reduced perfusion; tocolysis with terbutaline is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that precipitate labour with rapid delivery; tocolysis and bed rest is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Advise that uterine rupture with severe pain; immediate caesarean section is the correct tachysystole, precipitate labour & hypotonic contractions for this patient at this gestation
Hypotonic contractions lead to prolonged or slow progress of labour and are managed by augmentation with artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin. (Book p514)
All of the following are features of precipitate labour EXCEPT:
A latent phase lasting more than twenty hours
Delivery completed within about three hours of the first contraction
A higher risk of cervical, vaginal and perineal lacerations
A higher risk of postpartum haemorrhage from uterine atony
Precipitate labour is abnormally fast, so it tears the birth canal and leaves an exhausted uterus; a long latent phase is its opposite. (Book p514)
Which statement about Augmentation of labour — Kocher s forceps is TRUE?
Kocher's forceps, with a single tooth, rat-like teeth, a ratchet lock and transverse serrations is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Allis forceps, which are identified by several fine teeth on the jaws is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
A sponge holder, which is identified by its smooth, atraumatic jaws is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
An amnihook, which is identified by its single plastic hook is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Kocher's forceps has a single tooth at the tip with rat-like teeth, a ratchet lock and transverse serrations on the jaws. (Book p515)
Fill up: Rupture of membranes releases ______ which augments labour.
Rupture of membranes releases PGE2 which augments labour. (Book p515)

Match the augmentation of labour with the correct detail — 1) Absolute contraindications to ARM are: 2) In abruptio placentae, ARM is beneficial because it: 3) Indication for augmentation is slow progress (dilatation <1 … A) Maternal HIV, genital herpes infection, IUD of fetus B) Confirms the diagnosis and accelerates the process of labour C) Engaged: ARM → 30 min → oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin followed by ARM (↑ cord prolapse risk)
Absolute C/I: maternal HIV, genital herpes, IUD of fetus. Relative: polyhydramnios (↑ abruption risk) – controlled rupture with slow release. (Book p515)
Which statement about Augmentation of labour — ARM in abruptio is TRUE?
Confirms the diagnosis and accelerates the process of labour is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Stops the bleeding by tamponade is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Reduces risk of DIC directly is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Allows external cephalic version is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
ARM in abruptio placenta confirms diagnosis and accelerates labour. (Book p515)
Which statement about Augmentation of labour — Head engaged ARM is TRUE?
Engaged: ARM → 30 min → oxytocin; not engaged: oxytocin followed by ARM (↑ cord prolapse risk) is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Engaged: oxytocin → ARM; not engaged: ARM → oxytocin is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Both: ARM immediately followed by oxytocin is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Both: oxytocin only is the listed augmentation of labour as per the notes
Head engaged: ARM then oxytocin after 30 min; head not engaged: oxytocin first, then ARM to avoid cord prolapse. (Book p515)
A primigravida at 4 cm has contractions every six minutes lasting 25 seconds, with no cervical change over four hours, intact membranes and a normal CTG. What is the next step?
Amniotomy, reassess progress, then add oxytocin if contractions stay inadequate
Immediate caesarean section for failure to progress
Sedation and rest for twelve hours before any reassessment
Discharge home, because she cannot be in labour without cervical change
Inadequate contractions with intact membranes are augmented by amniotomy first, with oxytocin added only if contractions remain poor. (Book p515)
Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — Engagement descent flexion is TRUE?
Engagement → descent → flexion → internal rotation & crowning → extension → external rotation (restitution) → expulsion is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Descent → engagement → extension → flexion → internal rotation → expulsion → restitution is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Engagement → flexion → descent → extension → internal rotation → restitution → expulsion is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Flexion → engagement → descent → crowning → internal rotation → expulsion → extension is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Engagement, descent, flexion, internal rotation & crowning, extension, external rotation (restitution), expulsion. (Book p515)
Cardinal movements & the process of labour
Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — Normal delivery longitudinal is TRUE?
Longitudinal; cephalic; vertex is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Longitudinal; breech; sacrum is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Oblique; cephalic; brow is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Transverse; shoulder; acromion is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Normal delivery: longitudinal lie, cephalic presentation, vertex presenting part; head usually in LOT (LOT > LOA). (Book p516)
Cardinal movements & the process of labour

A 32-year-old primigravida at 9 weeks gestation presents for antenatal evaluation and counselling regarding cardinal movements & the process of labour. According to the notes, occiput rotates 2/8th of a circle (90°) at the ischial spine level: 45° by neck + 45° by shoulders. What is the most appropriate counselling for this patient?
Advise that 2/8th; ischial spine; 45°; 45° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 1/8th; ischial tuberosity; 45°; 0° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation
Advise that 3/8th; pelvic brim; 90°; 45° is the correct cardinal movements & the process of labour for this patient at this gestation

Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — Restitution untwists neck is TRUE?
Restitution: the neck untwists after delivery — external rotation: the shoulders turn one eighth of a circle is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution: the shoulders rotate one eighth — external rotation: the neck untwists is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution: the head extends as it is born — external rotation: the head flexes back is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution: descent through the cavity — external rotation: expulsion of the body is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Restitution untwists the neck after internal rotation, and external rotation then aligns the shoulders with the antero-posterior diameter. (Book p516)

Which statement about Cardinal movements & the process of labour — WHO recommends perineal is TRUE?
Perineal massage, warm towel, support the perineum, flex then extend the head is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes
Routine episiotomy, fundal pressure, and early maternal pushing efforts is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes

Vacuum extraction, perineal shaving, and routine episiotomy in all is the listed cardinal movements & the process of labour as per the notes

Match the cardinal movement with its description — 1) Engagement 2) Internal rotation 3) Extension … A) The occiput rotates anteriorly through about 45 degrees to lie behind the symphysis pubis B) The head is born by extending as it pivots under the symphysis pubis C) The biparietal diameter passes through the plane of the pelvic inlet

Vertex/sub-occipitobregmatic : vertex/occipito-frontal 11.5 cm : brow/mento-vertical → C-section : face/submento-vertical & submento-bregmatic
Fully flexed vertex – sub-occipitobregmatic; deflexed vertex – occipito-frontal 11.5 cm; brow – mento-vertical (C-section); face – submento-vertical/submento-bregmatic. (Book p517)

Fill up: The head is engaged when the ______ has passed through the pelvic inlet, after which only ______ of the head is palpable abdominally.
With the biparietal diameter through the brim, the sinciput is the only part easily felt above the symphysis. (Book p517)
Synclitic engagement means the sagittal suture lies in the transverse diameter of the pelvis:
Midway between the pubic symphysis and the sacral promontory
Closer to the pubic symphysis than to the sacral promontory
Closer to the sacral promontory than to the pubic symphysis
In the anteroposterior diameter, not the transverse diameter
Synclitic engagement means the sagittal suture lies in the transverse diameter midway between the pubic symphysis and the sacral promontory (LOT position). (Book p517)
Which of the following statements about asynclitism is TRUE?
The sagittal suture is deflected towards the sacrum or the symphysis so that one parietal bone leads, and mild degrees usually correct with good contractions
Asynclitism means the head is deflexed, so that the brow presents instead of the vertex
Every case of asynclitism needs caesarean section, since the head cannot negotiate the pelvis
In anterior asynclitism the posterior parietal bone always presents and always obstructs labour
Anterior asynclitism is Naegele obliquity and posterior is Litzmann obliquity; both usually correct with effective contractions and decent pelvis. (Book p517)
In ANTERIOR asynclitism the sagittal suture is deflected towards the ______, giving a ______ presentation, with ______ prognosis.
Anterior asynclitism: sagittal suture towards sacrum, anterior parietal presentation, better prognosis. (Book p518)
In POSTERIOR asynclitism the sagittal suture is deflected towards ______ and the presentation is ______.
Posterior asynclitism: suture deflected towards pubic symphysis, posterior parietal presentation. (Book p518)
The head of the baby is delivered by ______ in vertex and by ______ in breech/face.
Vertex – head delivered by extension; breech/face – by flexion. (Book p518)
Pain during the 1st stage arises from ______ (T10–L1) plus ______ (S2–S4).
1st stage: uterine contractions (T10–L1) + cervical dilatation (S2–S4). (Book p518)

Pain during the 2nd stage is from cervical dilatation (S2–S4) plus stretching of the perineum via the ______ nerve (______).
2nd stage: cervical dilatation S2–S4 + perineal stretch via pudendal nerve (S2–S4). (Book p518)

Epidural analgesia in labour – level of block : type of block.
T10 level; sensory and sympathetic block without motor block
T4 level; motor and sensory block without sympathetic block
L1 level; sympathetic block only, with no sensory block
S2 level; dense motor block with no sensory or sympathetic block
Epidural analgesia in labour aims at a T10 level with sensory and sympathetic block but no motor block. (Book p518)
Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
Drugs of choice for labour epidural and its effect on stages of labour:
Bupivacaine 0.625% or ropivacaine; shortens the 1st stage, prolongs the 2nd by 1 hour
Bupivacaine 0.5%; shortens both the 1st and the 2nd stage of labour
Lignocaine 2%; prolongs both the 1st and the 2nd stage of labour
Ropivacaine alone; no measurable effect on any stage of labour
The drugs of choice for labour epidural are bupivacaine 0.625% or ropivacaine; it shortens the first stage and prolongs the second stage by about 1 hour. (Book p518)
Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
Contraindication to epidural and the fact about C-section rate:
Anticoagulant in the 12-24 hours before labour; it does not raise the caesarean rate
Hypertension in labour; epidural doubles the caesarean section rate
Multiparity; epidural increases the forceps rate but not caesarean
Diabetes in pregnancy; epidural reduces the caesarean section rate
Epidural is contraindicated by anticoagulant use in the 12-24 hours before the onset of labour, and it does not increase the caesarean section rate. (Book p518)
Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
Fill up: First-stage labour pain is visceral and enters the cord at ______, while second-stage somatic perineal pain travels mainly in ______.
T10 to L1; the pudendal nerve (S2 to S4)
S2 to S4; T10 to L1
T6 to T8; the femoral nerve
L1 to L2; the obturator nerve
This is why an epidural covering T10 to L1 relieves contraction pain and a pudendal or low block is enough for the second stage. (Book p518)
Pain pathways of labour & epidural analgesia
Pudendal nerve block – site : ligament pierced : stage of pain relieved.
Pudendal block at ischial spine, piercing sacrospinous ligament, relieves 2nd stage pain. (Book p519)
Uses of pudendal block are ______; it does NOT block pain during ______.
Instrumental delivery and perineal or vaginal tear repair; cervical tears
Caesarean section and manual removal of the placenta; episiotomy
Repair of cervical tears; repair of the perineum afterwards
Suction evacuation of the uterus; instrumental delivery in labour
Pudendal block is used for instrumental delivery and repair of perineal or vaginal tears, but it does not block pain during repair of cervical tears. (Book p519)
Paracervical block – sites : sites avoided (and why) : duration.
2 or 4 o'clock and 8 or 10 o'clock : 3 and 9 o'clock (descending cervical artery) : 1–2 hrs
Sites 2/4 and 8/10 o'clock; avoid 3 and 9 o'clock because of the descending cervical artery; lasts 1–2 h. (Book p519)
Uses and contraindication of paracervical block:
Cervical repair and suction evacuation; contraindicated in labour (fetal bradycardia)
Instrumental delivery and perineal repair; contraindicated in labour (bradycardia)
Cervical repair and suction evacuation; contraindicated in hypertension
Caesarean section and suturing; contraindicated in multiple pregnancy
Paracervical block is used for repair of the cervix and for suction and evacuation, but is contraindicated in labour because it causes fetal bradycardia. (Book p519)
Prostaglandins act on ______ receptors present on ______ and are released ______.
G-protein cell membrane; myometrium and cervix; locally (paracrine)
G-protein coupled membrane receptors on myometrium and cervix; local paracrine release. (Book p519)
Match prostaglandin synthesis site to product and action – Decidua & myometrium : Amnion.
Decidua/myometrium → PGF2α (uterine action); amnion → PGE2 (cervical action). (Book p519)
Uses of prostaglandins in obstetrics include induction (sweeping fingers in internal os releases PGE2 → cervical ripening), and:
Augmentation of labour and management of PPH
Uses: induction, augmentation of labour, management of PPH. (Book p519)
All of the following statements about pudendal nerve block are true EXCEPT:
It abolishes the pain of uterine contractions in the first stage
It is given transvaginally with the needle directed just below the ischial spine
It provides perineal analgesia for an instrumental delivery
It does not relieve the pain of the contracting uterus
Pudendal block anaesthetises the perineum only; first-stage visceral pain needs a paracervical block or regional analgesia. (Book p519)
Induction of labour (IOL) is defined as ______; Bishop score checks ______ with a maximum of ______.
Initiation of uterine contractions in a patient not in labour; readiness of cervix and uterus before IOL; 13
Acceleration of established labour; fetal wellbeing; 10
Artificial rupture of membranes; pelvic adequacy; 9
IOL = initiation of contractions in a patient not in labour; Bishop score assesses cervix/uterus readiness; maximum 13. (Book p520)
Match the mnemonic 'Delhi Police Employed Special Commanders' to Bishop parameters:
Dilation, Presentation, Effacement, Softness, Cervix length
Delhi = dilation, Police = position, Employed = effacement, Special = station, Commanders = consistency. (Book p520)
Dilation: closed 0; 1–2 cm 1; 3–4 cm 2; >5 cm 3 – the most important parameter. (Book p520)
Scoring for POSITION of cervix (0 : 1 : 2) and its importance:
Posterior : middle : anterior; least important parameter
Position: posterior 0, middle 1, anterior 2; least important parameter. (Book p520)
Scoring for STATION of fetal head (0 : 1 : 2 : 3):
Station: above −2 = 0; −2 = 1; −1/0 = 2; below ischial spine = 3. (Book p520)
The simplified Bishop score uses ______ with a maximum of ______; the modified Bishop score replaces ______ with ______.
Dilation, effacement, station; 9; placement (position) of cervix; length of cervix by USG
Dilation, position, consistency; 7; station; fetal weight
Simplified: dilation + effacement + station (max 9). Modified: position replaced by USG cervical length. (Book p520)
Interpretation of the Bishop score — 5 or less : 6 or more : 9 or more.
5 or less: unripe and induction likely to fail — 6 or more: favourable — 9 or more: like spontaneous labour
5 or less: favourable — 6 or more: unripe — 9 or more: induction has already failed
5 or less: unripe — 6 or more: still unripe — 9 or more: favourable for induction
5 or less: vaginal delivery certain — 6 or more: favourable — 9 or more: unripe
A score of 5 or less predicts a failed induction, 6 or more is favourable, and 9 or more behaves like spontaneous labour. (Book p520)
Fill up: A Bishop score of ______ or more predicts a favourable induction, whereas a score of ______ or less means the cervix needs ripening first.
The score combines dilatation, effacement, station, consistency and position; a low score needs prostaglandin or mechanical ripening. (Book p520)
Match the methods – Cervical ripening : IOL : Augmentation.
Ripening: sweeping, mechanical, prostaglandins; IOL: mechanical, PG, oxytocin; augmentation: oxytocin, ARM
Ripening: oxytocin and ARM; IOL: sweeping of membranes; augmentation: prostaglandins
Ripening: prostaglandins only; IOL: ARM only; augmentation: oxytocin only
Ripening: mechanical methods; IOL: sweeping only; augmentation: prostaglandins

Cervical ripening uses sweeping of membranes, mechanical methods and prostaglandins; induction of labour uses mechanical methods, prostaglandins and oxytocin; augmentation uses oxytocin and ARM. (Book p520)
Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
Sweeping (stripping) of membranes – indication and principle:
Slightly dilated cervix; detaching membranes releases prostaglandins and ripens
Closed cervix; stretching the membranes releases oxytocin and ripens
A fully effaced cervix; sweeping deliberately ruptures the membranes
Any cervical state; sweeping mechanically dilates the cervical canal
Sweeping (stripping) of membranes is done when the cervix is slightly dilated; detaching the membranes from the cervix releases prostaglandins and ripens it. (Book p520)

Mechanical methods of IOL both ripen the cervix and induce labour; they are preferred in:
Mechanical methods ripen + induce and are preferred in a scarred uterus. (Book p521)

Transcervical Foley catheter for IOL – size, placement and volume:
A 16 F catheter in the endocervical canal with the bulb at the internal os, inflated with 30 mL saline
A 12 F catheter in the vagina with the bulb at the external os, inflated with 10 mL
A 20 F catheter passed into the uterine cavity and inflated with 60 mL
A 16 F catheter left in the posterior fornix and inflated with 50 mL
The bulb sits at the internal os and is inflated with 30 mL, stretching the cervix and stimulating prostaglandin release. (Book p521)
Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
Foley through the cervix, bulb inflated, saline infused extra-amniotically
Saline infused into the amniotic cavity through an amniocentesis needle
Saline infused into the bladder to compress the lower uterine segment
Intravenous saline with oxytocin running through the same catheter

EASI places a Foley in the endocervical canal, inflates the bulb and infuses normal saline at 30-40 ml/hr; the saline collects in the extra-amniotic space, separates the membranes and releases prostaglandins. (Book p521)
Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
Hygroscopic dilators used for IOL are exemplified by:
Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods

Match the method of induction with its description — 1) Membrane sweeping 2) Foley catheter with extra-amniotic saline infusion 3) Intracervical prostaglandin … A) A mechanical method that dilates the cervix and stimulates endogenous prostaglandin release B) A pharmacological ripening agent that also works when membranes have already ruptured C) A simple outpatient method that reduces the need for formal induction but may cause bleeding and discomfort
Sweeping is the simplest, mechanical methods suit women where prostaglandins are risky, and prostaglandins are the pharmacological ripeners. (Book p521)
Methods of induction: sweeping & mechanical methods
Prostaglandins for IOL are contraindicated in ______; risk of tachysystole ranks ______.
PG C/I: scarred uterus. Tachysystole: Cervidil > Cerviprime > misoprostol. (Book p521)
Misoprostol (PGE1) for IOL – dose, repetition, maximum and next step:
25 mcg oral or vaginal 3-6 hourly, max 6 doses; then oxytocin after a gap
50 mcg vaginally 2 hourly, max 4 doses; then caesarean section
100 mcg orally once only; then proceed to an oxytocin infusion
200 mcg vaginally 12 hourly, max 2 doses; then artificial rupture
Misoprostol (PGE1) for induction is 25 mcg oral or vaginal repeated 3-6 hourly (4 hourly), to a maximum of 6 doses; if no labour after a 4 hour gap, move to oxytocin. (Book p521)
Cerviprime gel (dinoprostone PGE2) – dose : site : repeat : maximum : storage.
0.5 mg : into cervix : 6 hourly : 3 doses, then oxytocin after 6 h : refrigerated
10 mg : posterior fornix : once : 1 : room temperature
Cerviprime 0.5 mg intracervical, 6-hourly, max 3 doses (oxytocin 6 h after last), refrigerated. (Book p522)
Cervidil (dinoprostone insert) – dose : release rate : site : duration.
10 mg : 0.3 mg/hr : posterior fornix : kept 12 h until labour
Cervidil 10 mg releasing 0.3 mg/hr, placed in posterior fornix, kept up to 12 h. (Book p522)
Oxytocin for IOL – if cervix is ripe ______; if not ripe ______.
Use oxytocin directly; ripen cervix then oxytocin
Ripe cervix → oxytocin directly; unripe → ripen then oxytocin. (Book p522)
5 U in 500 ml NS = 10 mIU/ml = 0.5 mIU/drop; max 52 drops/min (26 mIU/min)
10 U in 500 ml = 20 mIU/ml; max 20 drops/min
5 U in 100 ml = 50 mIU/ml; max 10 drops
2 U in 1 L = 2 mIU/ml; max 100 drops
5 U oxytocin + 500 ml NS → 10 mIU/ml → 0.5 mIU/drop; maximum 52 drops/min = 26 mIU/min. (Book p522)
Water intoxication with hyponatraemia when diluted in dextrose, and hypotension if the rate is too fast
Hypertension with hyperkalaemia from a rapid infusion of the drug
Reflex bradycardia with hyperglycaemia from the accompanying dextrose load
High fever with rigors and hypernatraemia from sodium retention

Fill up: Vaginal misoprostol for induction is used in low doses of about ______ microgram, and an oxytocin infusion is started at about ______ mU per minute.
Low-dose misoprostol and a low-dose oxytocin infusion that is titrated every 30 minutes minimise uterine hyperstimulation. (Book p522)
IOL is contraindicated wherever vaginal delivery is contraindicated. Which is NOT on the list?
Malpresentation – transverse lie, brow, mentoposterior face
Active genital herpes / contracted pelvis / CPD / cancer cervix

Listed: placenta previa, vasa previa, malpresentation, active herpes, contracted pelvis, CPD, cancer cervix, previous classical C-section/myomectomy, fetal distress, mono-mono/conjoined twins. (Book p522)

Which prior surgical histories contraindicate IOL?

MCMA twins and conjoined twins are C/I to IOL, as is fetal distress. (Book p522)

IOL for IUD of fetus – 20–28 weeks : >28 weeks.
20-28 weeks: misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV, then 400 mcg 3-hourly; over 28 weeks: ripen then oxytocin
20-28 weeks: oxytocin infusion alone; over 28 weeks: misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV 3-hourly
20-28 weeks: mifepristone alone; over 28 weeks: caesarean section in every case
20-28 weeks: misoprostol 25 mcg PV; over 28 weeks: misoprostol 800 mcg 3-hourly
For IUD, at 20-28 weeks give misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV then 400 mcg 3-hourly; beyond 28 weeks give 25 mcg misoprostol to ripen the cervix and then oxytocin. (Book p522)

All of the following are contraindications to induction of labour EXCEPT:
A previous uncomplicated vaginal delivery at term
Placenta previa with the placenta covering the internal os
A previous classical caesarean section with a vertical uterine scar
